name: Benin
instrument: Ministere de la Justice et de la Legislation, official explanatory publication on Loi n° 2022-32 du 20 decembre 2022 portant code de la nationalite beninoise ("Loi portant code de la nationalite beninoise en douze (12) questions"), section "Comment obtient-on la nationalite beninoise par attribution ?"
quote_original: tout enfant né au Bénin, quelle que soit la nationalité de ses parents, est
quote_translation: any child born in Benin, whatever the nationality of its parents, is presumed to be Beninese
notes: CAVEAT ON SOURCE TYPE — read before applying. The 1965 code was replaced by Loi n° 2022-32 du 20/12/2022 (JO n° 02 Ter, 25/01/2023). The statute itself is published officially at https://sgg.gouv.bj/doc/loi-2022-32/download and at textes.justice.bj (.../Z1PgfGYTcmiRyYeP78bi.pdf), but BOTH are image-only scans (18 pp, no text layer; pdftotext yields 18 bytes) and no OCR tool was available, so no article-level quote could be taken from the primary text. The quote above is from the Ministry of Justice and Legislation's own official publication on the new code, which is text-bearing and was verified verbatim on re-fetch. It states three attribution (droit du sol) cases: (a) any child born in Benin whatever its parents' nationality is presumed Beninese; (b) any child whose birth certificate was regularly drawn up in Benin; (c) a child found abandoned in Benin is presumed born in Benin provided it claims no other nationality. Case (a) plainly passes the two-known-foreign-parents test; case (c) alone is the foundling rule and was not counted. If the project will not cite a ministry explanatory publication as authority, downgrade this row to cannot_determine and flag Benin for an OCR pass on the scanned statute — the substance is not in doubt, only the citable text.

name: Kenya
quote_original: whether or not the person is born in Kenya, either the mother or father of the person is a citizen
notes: Confirms the recorded value. Art. 14(1)-(2) confer citizenship by birth on descent alone and expressly disclaim any territorial condition. The only territorial text in the article is art. 14(4), a foundling presumption for a child found in Kenya apparently under eight years of age whose nationality and parents are not known — not counted, per the brief. HOST WARNING: new.kenyalaw.org served this document successfully during research (1.45 MB, quote matched character-for-character) but returned HTTP 502 on three re-fetch attempts afterwards, including one with a 240 s timeout. The 502 is intermittent, not a dead host; if the verifier fails this row on HTTP status, retry rather than discarding it.

name: Azerbaijan
instrument: Law of the Republic of Azerbaijan No. 527-IQ of 30.09.1998 on citizenship of the Republic of Azerbaijan, art. 11(1) and art. 12 (third paragraph)
quote_translation: both of whose parents are stateless persons [— a child born on the territory of the Republic of Azerbaijan and both of whose parents are stateless persons is a citizen of the Republic of Azerbaijan]
notes: Art. 11(1): a person acquires citizenship when born ON THE TERRITORY of Azerbaijan (save the cases in art. 12 paras 1-2) or born of an Azerbaijani citizen — i.e. the statute's own primary rule is territorial with carve-outs, not descent-only. Art. 12 para 3 then confers citizenship on a child born on the territory both of whose parents are stateless. Art. 12 paras 1-2 exclude a child of two foreigners, and of one foreigner plus one stateless person, so the two-known-foreign-parents test fails and the limb is the statelessness safeguard, not unconditional jus soli. Art. 13 (child on the territory both of whose parents are unknown) is a foundling rule and was not counted. Quote deliberately kept to a fragment lying wholly on one source line — the surrounding sentence is broken by hard newlines in the published HTML. SOURCE NOTE: the human-facing page https://e-qanun.az/framework/3187 is a Next.js shell with no text; https://e-qanun.az/frameworks/3/f_3187.html returns 403; the frameworks.e-qanun.az subdomain above serves the same official consolidated text as HTML and returns 200. Document identity confirmed via the official API at https://api.e-qanun.az/framework/3187 (title, citation 527-IQ, acceptDate 30.09.1998, statusName Qüvvədədir = in force).

name: Belarus
instrument: Law of the Republic of Belarus of 1 August 2002 No. 136-Z on citizenship of the Republic of Belarus, art. 13
quote_original: являются лицами без гражданства, при условии, что ребенок родился на территории Республики Беларусь
quote_translation: are stateless persons, provided that the child was born on the territory of the Republic of Belarus
notes: Two territorial limbs in art. 13, both conditioned on birth on the territory. (i) parents (or the sole parent) temporarily or permanently residing in Belarus who are stateless — child born on the territory is a citizen (the quoted clause). (ii) parents permanently residing in Belarus who are FOREIGN CITIZENS — child born on the territory is a citizen where the states of which the parents are nationals do not grant it their citizenship. Limb (ii) is decisive: it applies to two known, identified foreign parents, so this passes the brief's test and is not a foundling artefact. The separate foundling rule (child on the territory whose parents are unknown) sits in the following paragraph and was not counted. Cited page is the pravo.by consolidated card, which carries the full running text plus an 'Изменения и дополнения' amendment history; the document does not print a single consolidation date, hence consolidated_as_of is empty.

name: Lithuania
instrument: Republic of Lithuania Law on Citizenship No. XI-1196, art. 14(1) (arts 15, 16 and 18(2) checked)
quote_original: Vaikas, kurio abu tėvai arba vienas iš jų yra Lietuvos Respublikos piliečiai,
quote_translation: A child both of whose parents, or one of whom, are citizens of the Republic of Lithuania,
notes: Confirms the recorded value, and it is the interesting negative in this batch. Lithuania DOES have a statelessness safeguard (art. 15) but it is NOT territorial: it applies to the child of stateless persons lawfully residing in Lithuania 'nesvarbu, ar jis gimė Lietuvos Respublikos teritorijoje, ar už jos ribų' — whether the child was born on the territory of the Republic of Lithuania or outside it. Birth on the territory is therefore not a condition of it, so it is not a territorial limb under the brief's definition. Art. 16 is a foundling rule (a child found or living on the territory both of whose parents are unknown is deemed born there) — not counted. Art. 18(2) gives a stateless person BORN in Lithuania a reduced 5-year naturalisation residence requirement — naturalisation, expressly excluded. SOURCE NOTE: the landing page https://e-seimas.lrs.lt/portal/legalAct/lt/TAD/TAIS.387811/asr returns 200 but renders only navigation, no article text, to a fetcher; the ISO_PDF URL above is the official consolidated edition ('Galiojanti suvestinė redakcija (nuo 2024-01-01)') and carries the full text. If the token segment in that path proves unstable, re-derive it from the landing page's download links.

name: Mongolia
instrument: Law of Mongolia on Citizenship (Харьяатын тухай хууль), art. 7
quote_original: Эцэг эх нь хоёулаа Монгол Улсын харьяат байсан үед төрсөн хүүхэд
quote_translation: A child born when both its parents were citizens of Mongolia
notes: Confirms the recorded value, but the article needs care because it is full of territorial language that does no territorial work. Art. 7(2) does turn on birth on Mongolian territory, but only where one parent is already a Mongolian citizen — a rule that turns on a parent's citizenship, expressly excluded. Art. 7(3) (one parent Mongolian, one stateless) applies regardless of place of birth. Art. 7(4) is a foundling rule (child present on the territory both of whose parents are not established) — not counted. Art. 7(5) is the near miss: a child born in Mongolia to two stateless parents permanently resident there MAY, on reaching 16 and at their own request, become a Mongolian citizen — a right to apply later in life, which the brief classifies as naturalisation rather than birthright, so it does not flip the verdict. Nothing in art. 7 gives citizenship to a child born in Mongolia to two known foreign parents. Text carries in-line amendment notes up to the law of 12 January 2024; the page prints no single consolidation date.

name: Tonga
instrument: Nationality Act, Cap. 25.06 (2016 Revised Edition), s. 2
quote_original: any person born in Tonga to a Tongan parent;
notes: Confirms the recorded value, and cleanly. Section 2 is an exhaustive list of persons deemed Tongan subjects: born in Tonga to a Tongan parent; born abroad of a Tongan father; born abroad of a Tongan mother; a non-Tongan who marries a Tongan and declares plus takes the oath; and any person naturalized under the Act. Sections 3-7 are repealed (Act 3 of 2007). There is no statelessness safeguard, no double jus soli, no residence limb and — unusually for this batch — not even a foundling provision. Note s. 2(a) mentions birth in Tonga but only in combination with a Tongan parent, so it is a descent rule, not a territorial limb. Published by the Attorney General's Office; the document states the revision year (2016) but no full date.

name: Uzbekistan
instrument: Law of the Republic of Uzbekistan No. ZRU-610 of 13 March 2020 on citizenship of the Republic of Uzbekistan, art. 14 (fifth paragraph); art. 15 checked
quote_original: Ребенок, родившийся на территории Республики Узбекистан, родители (одинокий родитель) которого являются лицами без гражданства
quote_translation: A child born on the territory of the Republic of Uzbekistan whose parents (sole parent) are stateless persons [acquires citizenship of the Republic of Uzbekistan by birth]
notes: Art. 14 confers citizenship by birth on descent 'independently of the place of birth' in its first three limbs, then adds the quoted territorial limb: a child BORN ON THE TERRITORY whose parents (or sole parent) are stateless acquires citizenship by birth. That is a statelessness safeguard conditioned on birth on the territory, so it qualifies. Art. 15 is the mirror exclusion — a child born on the territory whose parents are foreign citizens, or one foreign and one stateless, does NOT acquire citizenship by birth — so the two-known-foreign-parents test fails and the limb is not unconditional jus soli. The following paragraph of art. 14 (child on the territory both of whose parents are unknown) is a foundling rule and was not counted. Current instrument confirmed: ZRU-610 of 13.03.2020 replaced the 1992 law and entered into force 15 September 2020. Cite the /ru/ path; https://lex.uz/docs/4761986 serves the Uzbek text at the same id.

name: eSwatini
instrument: Constitution of the Kingdom of Swaziland Act, 2005, s. 43 (ss. 46, 47, 48 checked)
quote_original: A person born in Swaziland after the commencement of this Constitution is a citizen
notes: Confirms the recorded value. Section 43(1) reads in full that a person born in Swaziland after commencement is a citizen by birth ONLY IF at the time of birth the father was a citizen — the territorial words are there but the operative condition is paternal citizenship, so it is a descent rule. s. 43(2)-(3) cover birth abroad to a citizen father; s. 43(4) covers a child born outside marriage, unclaimed by the father, whose mother is a citizen; s. 43(5) covers adoption. s. 46 covers posthumous children; s. 48 deems birth aboard a Swazi-registered ship or aircraft to be birth in Swaziland (a deeming rule about location, not an independent limb). s. 47 is the foundling provision — a deserted child of not more than seven years found in Swaziland is deemed born there and treated as a citizen by birth — recorded as checked, not counted. Nothing confers citizenship on a child born in eSwatini to two known foreign parents. Official text on the Government of eSwatini portal; the PDF prints no consolidation date.

name: Namibia
instrument: Constitution of the Republic of Namibia, art. 4(1)(d) (art. 4(1)(b) is the pre-Independence analogue)
quote_original: ordinarily resident in Namibia at the time of the birth of such persons
notes: Strongest correction in this batch. Art. 4(1)(d) makes citizens by birth 'those born in Namibia after the date of Independence who do not qualify for citizenship under Sub-Article (c) hereof, and whose fathers or mothers are ordinarily resident in Namibia at the time of the birth of such persons' — a residence-based territorial limb that applies squarely to two known, identified foreign parents, subject only to exclusions for diplomats, career representatives of another country, members of a foreign police/military/security unit, and illegal immigrants. Those exclusions are themselves subject to a statelessness proviso: '(aa), (bb), (cc) and (dd) hereof will not apply to children who would otherwise be stateless' — hence the second limb type. This is not a foundling rule and not a descent rule; recording Namibia as jus_soli none is wrong. The quote is the operative residence clause and lies wholly on one line of the PDF text layer; the same words in art. 4(1)(b) are past tense ('were ordinarily resident') and are broken across lines, so this string is unique to art. 4(1)(d). SOURCE NOTE: the Ministry of Home Affairs copy at mha.gov.na 404s; this Ministry of Agriculture, Water and Land Reform copy is a live Namibian government host serving the official published Constitution with a text layer. Prefer a parliament.na copy if one is later found — note parliament.na's own 'Acts of Parliament' page links out to namiblii.org, which is in the excluded LII family.
